primary.key: Close to thy bosom am I, Soma, day and night. O Tawny-hued, for friendship sake. Surya himself refulgent with his glow have we o’ertaken in his course like birds.
primary.s: After a plea against the fiends that beset him, the singer speaks of his closeness to Soma; Sāyaṇa, on 9.107.20, takes the blazing sun as Soma himself in the highest place, whom the singers fly up to reach, as birds fly beyond the sun.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.107.20, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 400618 (2024)

basis.words: “सख्याय सख्यार्थं तव “ऊधनि समीपे “अहं रम इति शेषः । ते वयं “घृणा दीप्त्या “तपन्तं ज्वलन्तं “परः परमस्थानस्थितं “सूर्यं तदात्मकं त्वाम् “अति “पप्तिम । तत्र स्थितं त्वां प्राप्तुमतिपेतिम । कथमिव । “शकुनाइव । यथा सुपर्णादयः पक्षिणः सूर्यमतिगच्छन्ति तद्वत्
basis.gloss: For friendship, near you (I take delight, is understood). We have flown beyond the sun, blazing with radiance, standing in the highest place: you, who are of its nature. To reach you standing there we flew beyond. How? Like birds: as Suparṇa and the other birds go beyond the sun.

standby.key: Drive utterly away from us each demon, each voracious fiend, The godless and the false: keep sorrow far away.
standby.s: Closing a hymn that bids friends sing to the purified Soma, the singers ask him to keep every foe far off; Sāyaṇa, on 9.104.6, takes ‘the false’ as the double-dealer, holding truth and falsehood together, or guile outward and inward, and sorrow as sin.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 9.104.6, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 316086 (2021)

basis.words: “अत्रिणम् अदनशीलं “कं “चित् “रक्षसम् “अप युध्यस्व । कीदृशम् । “अदेवम् अदेवनशीलं “द्वयुं द्वयवन्तं सत्यानृतयुक्तं बाह्याभ्यन्तरमायायुक्तं वा । किंच “नः अस्माकम् “अंहः पापं चाप “युयोधि संप्रहर
basis.gloss: The devourer, any Rākṣasa whatever, fight him off. Of what kind? The godless, not given to worship; the dvayu, one who has doubleness, joined to truth and untruth, or possessed of guile both outward and inward. And strike away our aṃhas, our sin.

primary.key: When we most ignorant neglect the statutes of you, O Deities with whom is knowledge, Wise Agni shall correct our faults and failings, skilled to assign each God his fitting season.
primary.s: In a hymn asking Agni to worship the gods in season, the singers own their lapses; Sāyaṇa, on 10.2.4, takes Agni as Sviṣṭakṛt, maker of the well-offered rite, who knows what was neglected and fills up each rite with its fruit.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.2.4, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 343045 (2022)

basis.words: “प्रमिनाम प्रहिंसितवन्तः। भवत्सु जानत्सु नित्यनैमित्तिककर्माणि विलोपितवन्त इत्यर्थः । “विद्वान् एतत् सर्वं “जानानः अग्निः स्विष्टकृत् “तत् एतत् विश्वं सर्वं कर्मजातम् “आ “पृणाति आपूरयतु। फलसहितं करोत्वित्यर्थः
basis.gloss: We have violated: that is, while you who know look on, we have let the regular and occasional rites lapse. Knowing all this, Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, may he fill up all of it, the whole body of rites; the meaning is, may he make it complete with its fruit.

standby.key: A bard am I, my dad’s a leech, mammy lays corn upon the stones.
standby.s: In a hymn on the many trades by which people seek their living, the singer names his own household; Yāska, Nirukta 6.6, takes the bard as a maker of hymns, and the words for ‘dad’ and ‘mammy’ as father or son, and mother or daughter.
standby.src: Yāska, Nirukta 6.6, trans. Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921), archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask

basis.words: I am a bard, i.e. a composer of hymns. My father is a physician. The word tatah is a synonym of offspring, it means father or son. Stonegrmder, i.e. she who prepares barley meal. Nana, derived from (the root) aaon, means either mother or daughter.
basis.gloss: Sarup’s English of Yāska: the bard is a composer of hymns; tataḥ, a word for offspring, means father or son; the stone-grinder is she who prepares barley meal; nanā, from the root nam, means mother or daughter.

primary.key: Agni I deem my Kinsman and my Father, count him my Brother and my Friend for ever. I honour as the face of lofty Agni in heaven the bright and holy light of Surya.
primary.s: Asking Agni to bless the rite, the singer says what the god is to him; Sāyaṇa, on 10.7.3, reads the second line as a likeness: the singer tends the Āhavanīya fire, Agni’s face, as someone worships the sun’s bright disc to gain a wish.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.7.3, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 207987 (2019)

basis.words: “बृहतः महतः “अग्नेः “अनीकम् आहवनीयाख्यं मुखं “सपर्यं परिचरामि । तत्र लुप्तोपममेतत् । “दिवि द्युलोके स्थितं “यजतं यष्टव्यं पूजनीयं “सूर्यस्य संबन्धि “शुक्रं दीप्तिमत् मण्डलं यथा कश्चिदभिप्रेतार्थसिद्धये आराधयति तद्वत्
basis.gloss: The face of the great Agni, the one called the Āhavanīya, I serve. Here the word of likeness is left out: as someone, to gain a desired end, worships the bright disc of the sun, standing in heaven and worthy of worship, so.

standby.key: Like thieves who risk their lives and haunt the forest, the twain with their ten girdles have secured him.
standby.s: Near the close of a hymn praising Agni as a spring in the desert, the singer turns to a likeness; Yāska, Nirukta 3.14, takes the two thieves as the two arms that bring forth fire by friction, and the girdles as ten fingers.
standby.src: Yāska, Nirukta 3.14, trans. Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921), archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask

basis.words: As two thieves, who risk their lives and haunt the forest, have secured (their victim) with ten fingers.^ Who risk their lives, who give up their lives.^*^ Who haunt the forest, i. e. who frequent the forest : the author compares the two arms, wdiich produce fire by (the process of) friction, with two thieves.
basis.gloss: Sarup’s English of Yāska: the two thieves have secured their victim with ten fingers; they give up their lives and frequent the forest; the author compares the two arms, which produce fire by friction, with two thieves.

primary.key: The Sun receive thine eye, the Wind thy spirit; go, as thy merit is, to earth or heaven.
primary.s: At the pyre, having asked Agni to bear the dead to the Fathers, the singer turns to the dead man; Sāyaṇa, on 10.16.3, takes the spirit as the breath, going to the outer wind, and merit as good deeds, whose fruit he goes to enjoy.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.16.3, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 333348 (2022)

basis.words: हे प्रेत त्वदीयं चक्षुः इन्द्रियं सूर्यं गच्छतु प्राप्नोतु । आत्मा प्राणः वातं बाह्यं वायुं गच्छतु । अपि च त्वमपि धर्मणा सुकृतेन तत्फलं भोक्तुं द्या च । अत्र चशब्दो विकल्पार्थे । द्युलोकं वा पृथिवीं च पृथिवीं वा गच्छ प्राप्नुहि
basis.gloss: O departed one, let your eye, the sense, go to the sun; the ātman, that is the breath, to the outer wind. And you too, by dharman, that is by good deeds, to enjoy their fruit, go to heaven or (the word ca here means or) to earth: reach it.

standby.key: Guard of the world, whose cattle ne’er are injured, may Pusan bear thee hence, for he hath knowledge. May he consign thee to these Fathers’ keeping, and to the gracious Gods let Agni give thee.
standby.s: Turning from the tale of Tvastar’s daughter to the funeral rite, the singer addresses the departed; Yāska, Nirukta 7.9, takes Pusan as the sun, guardian of all created beings, and finds it doubtful whether he or Agni gives the dead to the Fathers.
standby.src: Yāska, Nirukta 7.9, trans. Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921), archive.org nighantuniruktao00yask

basis.words: i.e. he, the sun, is indeed the guardian of all created beings, forthwith cause thee to move from this world. The third verse 'May he hand thee over to the manes', is doubtful. According to some It refers to Pusan, (mentioned) in the preceding hemistich ; a^jcording to others this extols Agni, (mentioned) subsequently.
basis.gloss: Sarup’s English of Yāska: Pūṣan, that is the sun, is the guardian of all created beings; the third quarter, ‘may he hand thee over to the manes’, is doubtful: some refer it to Pūṣan, named in the half-verse before, others take it as praising Agni, named after it.

primary.key: As the days follow days in close succession, as with the seasons duly come the seasons, As each successor fails not his foregoer, so form the lives of these, O great Ordainer.
primary.s: In a hymn that sends Death away from the living, the singer turns to the Ordainer; Sāyaṇa, on 10.18.5, takes the successor who does not forsake his foregoer as a son who does not leave his father by dying first.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.18.5, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 353436 (2022)

basis.words: “यथा च “पूर्वं पूर्वकालीनं पितरम् “अपरः अर्वाक्कालीनः पुत्रः “न “जहाति न परित्यजति पूर्वमरणेन । “एव “एवं तेनैवोक्तप्रकारेण हे “धातः सर्वेषां धारयितरेतन्नामक देव “एषाम् अस्मत्कुलीनानां जीवानाम् “आयूंषि जीवनानि “कल्पय समर्थय
basis.gloss: And as the later one, the son born after, does not abandon the former, the father born before, by dying first: just so, in the very way described, O Dhātṛ, god of that name who sustains all, arrange the lives, the living spans, of these living members of our family.

standby.key: SEND us a good and happy mind, send energy and mental power.
standby.s: Opening a hymn to Soma, the singer asks first for gifts of mind; Sāyaṇa, on 10.25.1, takes the ‘energy’ as the inner self, to be made a doer of good, and the ‘mental power’ as understanding bent on good resolve.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.25.1, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 321581 (2021)

basis.words: अस्माकं मनः शुभसंकल्पं कुर्वित्यर्थः । तथा “दक्षमुत दक्षमपि । 'दक्ष वृद्धौ' । वृद्धं सर्वव्यापिनमन्तरात्मानमपि भद्रं शुभकारित्वलक्षणं प्रापय । अस्माकमन्तरात्मानं शुभकारिणं कुर्वित्यर्थः। उतापि च “क्रतुं प्रज्ञानं भद्रं शुभाध्यवसायलक्षणं प्रापय । शुभाध्यवसायिनं कुर्वित्यर्थः
basis.gloss: The meaning is: make our mind one of good resolve. So too dakṣa (from the root dakṣ, to grow): bring the grown, all-pervading inner self to what is good, marked by doing good; the meaning is, make our inner self a doer of good. And kratu, understanding: bring it to what is good, marked by good resolve; the meaning is, make it resolved on good.

primary.key: A man should think on wealth and strive to win it by adoration on the path of Order, Counsel himself with his own mental insight, and grasp still nobler vigour with his spirit.
primary.s: After a prayer to pass beyond all troubles, the hymn to all the gods turns to a man’s duties; Sāyaṇa, on 10.31.2, takes the counsel as meditating on the gods at the offering, and the nobler vigour as the all-pervading self, grasped in meditation.
primary.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.31.2, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 202075 (2019)

basis.words: “उत अपि च “स्वेन आत्मीयेन “क्रतुना प्रज्ञानेन । मनसेत्यर्थः । “सं “वदेत । संवादोऽत्र समाध्यानमुच्यते । हविर्गृहीत्वा वषट्करिष्यन् विश्वान् देवान् मनसाध्यायेदित्यर्थः । विश्वेषां देवानां यागानन्तरं च तत्प्रसादात् “श्रेयांसम् अतिशयेन प्रशस्यमात्मानं “दक्षं प्रवृद्धं सर्वव्यापिनं “मनसा ध्यानसाधनेनान्तःकरणेन “जगृभ्यात् गृह्णीयात्
basis.gloss: And with his own kratu, his understanding, that is, his mind, let him converse: conversing here means meditating; the meaning is, taking up the oblation and about to say vaṣaṭ, let him meditate in his mind on all the gods. And after the sacrifice to all the gods, by their grace, let him grasp the most excellent self, dakṣa, grown great and all-pervading, with the mind, the inner organ that is the means of meditation.

standby.key: Speed happily those, as Surya ends his journey, who meet his wish as bridegrooms meet their spouses; Men who present, O Indra strong by nature, with food the many songs that tell thy praises.
standby.s: Asking what draws Indra to his worshippers, the singer prays for them; Sāyaṇa, on 10.29.5, reads the prayer as asking Indra to bring the worshippers to the end of the round of births, as the sun brings the yogin to the far shore.
standby.src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 10.29.5, sa.wikisource (the printed edition is not named), revision 208026 (2019)

basis.words: “सूरः सूर्यः “अर्थं “न यथार्तारं गन्तारं योगिनमनुगृह्णन् “पारं संसारस्यान्तमपवर्गं गमयति तथा हे इन्द्र त्वं यजमानान् संसारस्यान्तं “प्रेरय गमय
basis.gloss: As the sun, favouring the one who goes, the yogin, brings him to the far shore, the end of saṃsāra, release: so, Indra, send the sacrificers on to the end of saṃsāra.
